result_semantic_payload.summary: The hypothesis that employee 'lihua' exported the customer database on 2024-05-10 is NOT supported by the recorded evidence. The customer export that occurred on 2024-05-10 (01:03:22–01:03:40) was performed by the dedicated non-interactive service account 'svc_export' as part of the scheduled 'nightly_export' job. The scheduler definition at /scheduler/jobs.conf explicitly binds job 'nightly_export' to run_as 'svc_export' with a 23:55 daily schedule, and /export/app.log records 'SCHEDULE job=nightly_export account=svc_export triggered' at 2024-05-09 23:55:01 followed by two EXPORT lines under account=svc_export writing to /backup/customers_20240510.tar.gz. The README.txt describes svc_export as 'a dedicated non-interactive service account used by scheduled jobs.' The only entries mentioning 'lihua' in the log are two FAILED login attempts at 2024-05-10 01:47:11 and 01:47:59 from IP 198.51.100.44 (reason=password), which occurred AFTER the export completed and never succeeded. No evidence in the scope attributes any export action to lihua.

claim_candidates.text: The customer database export on 2024-05-10 was executed by service account 'svc_export', not employee 'lihua'.

The export was triggered by the scheduled 'nightly_export' job (schedule 23:55 daily, run_as svc_export), consistent with the 2024-05-09 23:55:01 SCHEDULE trigger line and the 2024-05-10 01:03:22 EXPORT line.
The export produced /backup/customers_20240510.tar.gz containing 184,112 rows of the 'customers' dataset and completed successfully in 18 seconds.

Employee 'lihua' had no successful authentication and no export activity in the recorded evidence; only two FAILED login attempts from 198.51.100.44 at 2024-05-10 01:47:11 and 01:47:59 (reason=password) appear, both occurring after the export completed.
The analyst's hypothesis that lihua performed the export is contradicted by the evidence and should be rejected; attribution should be to the scheduled svc_export job.

The two failed lihua logins from 198.51.100.44 shortly after the export warrant follow-up to determine whether they indicate a separate credential-guessing attempt, but they cannot be linked to the export itself.

limitations: Task metadata reports platforms=[] and source_scopes=[]; the 'windows' scope requested in the delegation contains no Windows-native evidence (no registry, Prefetch, Amcache, Event Logs), so Windows-specific corroboration (prefetch/amcache) required by the profile is unavailable.
File mtimes/ctimes all equal the imaging timestamp 1790594134; original modification times cannot be recovered from the metadata exposed here.
app.log is a single 440-byte file with only 5 lines covering 2024-05-09 23:55:01 through 2024-05-10 01:47:59; earlier/later activity and any other accounts are not represented.
No audit trail of who created or modified /scheduler/jobs.conf is available; the nightly_export schedule cannot be independently verified as unchanged.

The failed lihua logins from 198.51.100.44 cannot be linked to any export action from the available evidence, but no external network or authentication-source logs are present to confirm or deny a separate intrusion attempt.
warnings: The analyst hypothesis is refuted by the evidence; the export is attributable to the scheduled svc_export job, not to lihua.
Scope mismatch: the delegation requested 'windows' scope, but the registered task exposes no Windows platform evidence — findings are based on generic file evidence only.
